Pursuant to the mandate of the Court of Appeals,
IT IS HEREBY ORDERED that:
1. The approval by the Department of the Interior on June 14, 1972, of the coal mining leases, and approval on November 26, 1974, of the amended coal mining leases, between Westmoreland Resources and the Crow Tribe of Indians were major federal actions which required the preparation of an environmental impact statement that satisfies the requirements of the National Environmental Policy Act, 42 U.S.C. 4321, at seq., relating to the mining of coal in all of the lands subject to the leases;
2. The environmental impact statement prepared in conjunction with the five-year mining plan on the 770-acre tract, which is part of the leased area, is not adequate under the National Environmental Policy Act to support approval of these leases;
3. The Secretary of the Interior must prepare an environmental impact statement satisfying the requirements of the National Environmental Policy Act on these leases and then, on the basis of that statement, fully reconsider whether to approve the leases without giving consideration to investments or commitments made by Westmoreland Resources under the five-year plan on the 770-acre tract;
